Detroit is a 3.5-point favorite in the latest Lions vs. Panthers odds from DraftKings Sportsbook, and the Over/Under on the game total is set at 47.5 points. They also placed both starting cornerbacks on IR, so things could be dicey against this explosive Lions offense. It was supposed to dump rain all day Sunday in North Carolina, but we're now staring down just some chill in the air and what should be a fun one. The Lions' last appearance in prime time cashed everyone out with the explosive matchup against the Bills . I'm not expecting Carolina to perform like Buffalo did, but the Panthers are highly susceptible to being dragged into shootouts if their opponent starts to sling the ball around. Given the dearth of defensive backfield talent out there for Carolina, I fully expect the Lions to take advantage and throw the ball downfield. Carolina should be able to answer and we should get points galore. He broke out in Week 2 with a pair of scores then was rewarded with eight targets in Week 3 against the Browns . I'd expect him to see close to that many again Sunday night, making this number just way too low for how much Bryce looks his way, especially if Jalen Coker ends up inactive tonight. Jahmyr Gibbs Over 37.5 receiving yards (-115, DraftKings) Gibbs is the unquestioned best running back in football right now and has really rewarded anyone who took him first overall in fantasy. But he's not just a great runner, he's also an elite receiver, and in a game that should be a shootout with Jared Goff looking to exploit the Panthers defense, I'd expect Gibbs to be plenty involved in the pass game as well. 40 receiving yards feels very, very doable for the superstar. But he's been just OK thus far, and as such we're getting a great price. Jamo can score from anywhere, should get plenty of short-yardage looks with screens and the like and also is the ultimate deep threat going against a really depleted secondary. Brycen Tremayne (+360, DraftKings) This is a bit of a longshot, but, again, we're thinking Jalen Coker won't play in this game. That's going to likely slide Tremayne into a starting role opposite of Tetairoa McMillan at wide receiver, and if this is a shootout, Young is going to have to throw a lot. There's a good chance Tremayne gets lost in the sauce near the end zone, setting him up as a nice high-value play to score. By Zachary Cohen - October 3, 2026 87595 X Facebook Email It’s time for Week 4 of the 2026 NFL season. I strongly suggest you check out the Week 4 NFL Betting Hub , where you’ll find all of the features and picks from my talented co-workers. On top of that, we never stop pumping out good NFL content on our live shows . That’s the beauty of being a subscriber. As a company, we’re relentless in our effort to get you prepared for these games. With that out of the way, let’s get into the fun stuff. Keep reading for my Week 4 NFL best bets and Week 4 NFL player props. MORE: Check out our Pro Picks page for NFL best bets from all of our analysts Indianapolis Colts vs. Washington Commanders – 9:30 am ET (London) The Colts might be down Alec Pierce, but I like the way this offense operates. Indianapolis lost a tough one in Kansas City two weeks ago, but the team put up 30 points against a Chiefs team that is sixth in the NFL in EPA/Play Allowed (-0.077) this year. It’s just hard to stop the Colts once Jonathan Taylor gets going on the ground. He puts Indianapolis in a ton of manageable third-and-short situations. Of course, Washington is a top-five team in Rush EPA/Play Allowed (-0.318) right now. The Commanders have done a good job of stuffing opponents thus far. But they haven’t seen an offensive line quite like this, and they haven’t faced a running back this efficient. Also, if Washington is selling out to stop the run, Daniel Jones should be able to do some real damage through the air — especially when looking Josh Downs’ way. I also happen to love the Commanders to put up points on the Colts defense. Marcus Mariota is an excellent backup, so Washington’s offense isn’t going to completely stall out with Jayden Daniels injured. Mariota played well in relief of Daniels two games ago, and he threw for three touchdowns in his start last week. He’s accurate, he understands the offense, and he’s still a threat with his legs. He’s also up against a Colts defense that is 30th in the NFL in EPA/Play Allowed (0.124). Honestly, this might not seem like the most enticing standalone game, but I think it’s going to deliver some early-morning excitement. Two shaky defenses should mean a real shot at a shootout. Also, since 2024, the Over is 15-1 when Washington is an underdog of 3.5 to 9.5 points. The average total points scored in such games is 58.2 points per game. Bet: Over 46.5 (-115) Dallas Cowboys at Houston Texans – 1:00 pm ET We haven’t seen anything from Houston this season, but a bounce-back performance should be coming soon. I don’t expect the Texans to completely stifle a good Cowboys offense, but I do know that Houston is much better than its No. 19 ranking in EPA/Play Allowed (0.012) this year. This is a Texans defense that has been elite for years, and none of the moves made in the offseason should have resulted in this type of drop-off. That said, look for Houston to start playing some much better defense, and we could see it start with a decent showing against Dak Prescott and Co. I also love any offense in a matchup with the Cowboys defense, as Dallas is at the bottom of the league in EPA/Play Allowed (0.193). The Cowboys made some moves to address their miserable defense from last season, but it doesn’t look like any of them have worked. So, this should be a pretty strong matchup for CJ Stroud. Of course, Stroud has issues as a passer, but he’s reliable when he has time to get his feet set. That’s a good thing as Stroud prepares to face a defense that is 31st in Pass Rush Win Rate (40%). He should have plenty of time. This is also a massive desperation spot for Houston. I can’t imagine Dallas is thrilled to be sitting at 1-2 right now, but Houston’s season might be over if the team drops this one to fall to 0-4. Bet: Texans ML (-136) Arizona Cardinals at New York Giants – 1:00 pm ET Jameis Winston has been pretty buttoned up since taking over for Jaxson Dart, but I imagine he’ll be slinging it around a bit here. This season, the Cardinals are allowing 247.0 passing yards per game, and their two starting corners have an average PFF grade of 52.1. New York has been conservative with Winston so far, opting to lean heavily into a ground-and-pound approach. However, the Giants need to play the matchup, and this is one that calls for some passing. Arizona is a top-10 team in pass frequency. So, if the Cardinals are letting Jacoby Brissett air it out, the Giants will have no choice but to let Winston do the same. I know Winston hasn’t yet thrown for a score, and he also hasn’t eclipsed 118 passing yards in a game. But we all know that Winston is a gunslinger, and you don’t have to go back too far to find a box score in which he threw for 366 yards and two touchdowns. That was November 23, 2025, when Winston got involved in a shootout with the Lions. Week 4 arrives with no shortage of NFL betting action, major storylines and roster shakeups, which means we're back with another look at the most notable angles from the weekly slate. Between prediction markets opening a new way of sports trading and sportsbooks ramping up the promos, NFL betting is at an all-time high this season and we are here to make sure you don't miss a beat as we head into Week 4. Find the narrative, check the data and let the numbers inside our NFL predictions do the rest while you sit back and take in every game this season. Below, we break down the week's biggest storylines, our model's top spread and moneyline picks, and the players, markets and scenarios most worth your attention. Three storylines to watch in Week 4 1. Sunday morning football from London Set your alarms! We've had two international games already this season, but they haven't messed with the broadcast schedule as Rams-Niners from Australia was our TNF game, and Cowboys-Ravens this past weekend was on in the Sunday afternoon window. Colts vs. Commanders will be the first overseas game with a Sunday morning kickoff, getting udnerway at 9:30 AM ET from Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London. Both teams are coming off Week 3 wins and big improvements, with Washington unlocking the ceiling of their offense and the Colts defense finally showing up after giving up over 70 points through two games. Early predictions for the Dimers model give a slight lean to the over 46.5 at 51.2%, and a 63.0% win probability for Indianapolis. Both RBs, Jonathan Taylor (66,1%) and Jacory Croskey-Merritt (55.2%), have strong TD probabilities and the top WRs for both teams, Josh Downs and Terry McLaurin , project to clear 60 receiving yards. 2. First place up for grabs in AFC West Could the Raiders really go 4-0? Las Vegas has rolled to three wins early this season behind QB Kirk Cousins , and head coach Klint Kubiak . At +800, they're tied atop the AFC West standings with the Chiefs who are -125. Both teams face off in Week 4. In the Patrick Mahomes era (since 2018), the Raiders have 3 wins against the Chiefs. The Raiders are 4.5-point underdogs this week, with a 51.6% chance the Chiefs cover on the way to a win. But, the Dimers model predicts the Raiders to put up a fight; both TE Brock Bowers and RB Ashton Jeanty are over a 43% chance for a touchdown, the second and third-most likely players to score in the game. The key for Vegas will be containing Chiefs RB Kenneth Walker , who's projected for 87 rushing yards (third-most of the week) and a 53.6% TD probability, the latter of which does rank outside our top 10 RBs for the week. 3. Next man up: RB edition Week 2 was the QBs, but Week 3 saw multiple starting RBs go down with injury. Breece Hall (Jets), De'Von Achane (Dolphins) and Travis Etienne Jr. (Saints) all left their games and are et to miss varying degrees of time. Achane is out for the season with a torn ACL, while Etienne (hamstring) and Hall (quad) are more week-to-week. In Miami, Ollie Gordon and Jaylen Wright are behind Achane, but Wright is day-to-day with his own foot injury, and Gordon projects to lead the backfield with a 25.2% TD probability and 33.3 rushing yards. Braelon Allen is the next man up behind Hall, and after scoring in Week 2, projects for 54.8 rushing yards and a substantial 47.4% TD probability vs. the Bears. In New Orleans, the committee of veteran Alvin Kamara and career backup Kendre Miller will split duties, with Kamara projected to lead with 35.9 rushing yards, 15.1 receiving yards and a 32.7% TD probability. These signals are the first to look for when researching a weekly NFL slate, as it shows where our model has proven to be most accurate . Due to the launch of our brand-new NFL model, only props have Sweet Spots that have carried over from last season. Once we have enough bets in the bank, you'll find game lines here as well. Two takeaways heading into Week 4: our top market of Rushing Yards has ticked up another 2.2% since Week 3, and 2+ touchdowns have made their way into positive ROI over 100 bets dating back to last season. This week, there are over 20 players with an edge to score twice. Players to watch in Week 4 These are players who need to be on your radar, whether in fantasy leagues or for player prop betting. Last week, we looked at Christian Watson (scored for the third straight game), CeeDee Lamb (7 catches, 112 yards) and Derrick Henry (two touchdowns). 1. Derrick Henry (Ravens) Yeah, we're looking at Derrick Henry again. Why, you ask? He's playing his former franchise, the Titans for the first time. Tennessee is as bad as ever and have the 24th-ranked rushing defense this season, allowing 126.3 yards per game and 3 rushing touchdowns. King Henry has six rushing touchdowns this season and enters this game with the highest touchdown probability of a player yet this season at 71.1% and his 12.9% chance for 3 or more touchdowns is a full 2% higher than any other player. 2. Tetairoa McMillan (Panthers) Panthers WR Tetairoa "Tet" McMillan has yet to find the end zone this season, and is coming off his first disappointing game of the year, catching just 2 of 5 targets for 17 yards. After a 1,000-yard, 7-TD rookie season, expectations have been high for the second-year wideout, but he hasn't scored. In Week 4 vs. the Lions, Tet projects for the 9th-most receiving yards of the week at 70.1 and a 28.2% TD probability. No team in the NFL has given up more passing yards than the Detroit Lions at 979 , 104 more than the next team, and their 9 passing TDs are the second-most allowed. 3. David Montgomery (Texans) After a 3-TD Week 1 performance, David Montgomery looked like a league-winner in fantasy and a top betting target. He has 42 rushing yards and no scores since then. Fortunately, he has the cure for all production ailments on tap in Week 4, a matchup with the Cowboys defense. Dimers' top-projected running backs in Week 4. Already bottom-tier and now dealing with injuries, the Cowboys have given up the second-most rushing yards this season at 539 (over 100 more than Denver at third-most) and 3 rushing touchdowns. Montgomery's rushing projection is solid but modest, though 69.1 yards would be the highest for him this season, and the fourth-highest TD probability of the week at 63.7%, with a substantial 26.9% probability to score twice, higher than OPOY favorites Bojan Robinson and Jaxon Smith-Njigba. I'm looking at you, Texans and Chargers. There are also a few early contenders that I'm thinking might be pretenders. New York Giants, anyone? Here's where I'm putting my money in Week 5. Buccaneers @ Cowboys The Cowboys are once again a machine on offense, sitting near the top of the league by averaging over 30 points per game. I expect another big offensive performance Thursday night against the reeling Bucs. Hill's Pick: Cowboys Over 29.5 (-115) Eagles vs. Jaguars The Eagles are a complete mess offensively, and have key injuries to many of their best players. I don’t think that gets fixed overnight. Hill's Pick: Eagles Under 17.5 (-140) Bears @ Packers A genius. A wizard. Bears head coach Ben Johnson is worthy of all the accolades, winning three games this year with three different starting quarterbacks. That being said, being a road favorite at Lambeau with a backup quarterback has me looking at the Packers. Hill's Pick: Packers +1.5 (-110) Texans @ Titans It’s now or never for the Texans, who can ill afford another loss and an 0-5 start. I’ll go Over the total here considering the Texans look to be improved on offense while their intimidating defense has regressed significantly in 2026. Hill's Pick: Over 38.5 (-110) Bengals @ Dolphins The Dolphins are 0-4 but have been feisty and rather competitive the last couple of weeks against the Chiefs and Vikings. The heat in Miami is a tough obstacle for visitors this time of year. I like the home team to keep it close. Hill's Pick: Dolphins +7.5 (-110) Raiders @ Patriots The Patriots perhaps saved their season last week with a clutch win in Buffalo. They are 2-2 despite having the most turnovers in the NFL (12). The Raiders have 10 takeaways, also the most in the NFL. There is a lot of randomness when it comes to turnovers. I’ll back the Patriots here, who are due for some better turnover luck. Hill's Pick: Patriots -3.5 (-110) Vikings @ Saints The Vikings have issues on offense but do have an excellent kicker in Will Reichard. Reichard is 12-for-12 this year on field goals, averaging three makes per game. Against a shaky Saints defense, I expect him to make a couple of field goals. Hill's Pick: Will Reichard Over 1.5 Made FGs (-150) Browns @ Jets Browns rookie receiver KJ Concepción had a breakout game last week with five catches for 64 yards on eight targets. The week before, he had nine targets against the Panthers. His prop is set at 40.5 this week, which seems a bit low. Hill's Pick: KJ Concepción Over 40.5 Receiving Yards (-109) Colts @ Steelers The Colts are playing a road game immediately after traveling back from London last week. The Steelers are home off of extra rest after losing to the rival Browns last week. The rest/travel situation heavily favors the home team. Hill's Pick: Steelers -2.5 (-110) Giants @ Commanders The Giants have hung on for close home wins vs. a soft schedule to get to 3-1, but I’ll take them +3.5 this week against a Commanders team that will send injury-prone quarterback Jayden Daniels back onto the field, with perhaps a cumbersome brace on his left elbow. Hill's Pick: Giants +3.5 (-110) Broncos @ Chargers It hasn’t been pretty for the disappointing Chargers, but they battled in the last two weeks, losing one-score games at Buffalo and Seattle. Eventually, they will win a game, and it might not be this week, but getting 3.5 at home against an underwhelming Broncos team is too good to pass up. Hill's Pick: Chargers +3.5 (-110) Lions @ Cardinals The Lions are 4-0 on the Over this year. They are very good on offense but abysmal defensively. I’ll stick with their Overs until proven otherwise. Hill's Pick: Over 54.5 (-110) 49ers @ Seahawks These teams have not played this year, but they have met twice in 2026. Seattle won both of those games by a combined score of 54-9. I’ll take the Seahawks to win again. Hill's Pick: Seahawks -3 (-110) Ravens @ Falcons Last week, I suggested taking Falcons’ star back Bijan Robinson Over his rushing prop and it cashed easily. It’s not fun, but this week I’ll take a shot on the Under, as Robinson draws a solid Baltimore rush defense that is allowing under four yards per carry. Hill's Pick: Bijan Robinson Under 89.5 Rushing Yards (-110) Bills @ Rams An exciting game on Monday night, but there are whispers that Bills quarterback Josh Allen is battling a knee injury. Allen only ran for four yards last week, so with his prop set at 36.5, I’ll go Under. I’ll back the Patriots here, who are due for some better turnover luck. Hill's Pick: Patriots -3.5 (-110) The Vikings have issues on offense but do have an excellent kicker in Will Reichard. Reichard is 12-for-12 this year on field goals, averaging three makes per game. Against a shaky Saints defense, I expect him to make a couple of field goals. Hill's Pick: Will Reichard Over 1.5 Made FGs (-150) Browns rookie receiver KJ Concepción had a breakout game last week with five catches for 64 yards on eight targets. The week before, he had nine targets against the Panthers. His prop is set at 40.5 this week, which seems a bit low. Hill's Pick: KJ Concepción Over 40.5 Receiving Yards (-109)

The Giants have hung on for close home wins vs. a soft schedule to get to 3-1, but I’ll take them +3.5 this week against a Commanders team that will send injury-prone quarterback Jayden Daniels back onto the field, with perhaps a cumbersome brace on his left elbow. Hill's Pick: Giants +3.5 (-110) It hasn’t been pretty for the disappointing Chargers, but they battled in the last two weeks, losing one-score games at Buffalo and Seattle. Eventually, they will win a game, and it might not be this week, but getting 3.5 at home against an underwhelming Broncos team is too good to pass up. Hill's Pick: Chargers +3.5 (-110) The Lions are 4-0 on the Over this year. They are very good on offense but abysmal defensively. I’ll stick with their Overs until proven otherwise. Hill's Pick: Over 54.5 (-110) These teams have not played this year, but they have met twice in 2026.

Bears head coach Ben Johnson is worthy of all the accolades, winning three games this year with three different starting quarterbacks. That being said, being a road favorite at Lambeau with a backup quarterback has me looking at the Packers. Hill's Pick: Packers +1.5 (-110) It’s now or never for the Texans, who can ill afford another loss and an 0-5 start. I’ll go Over the total here considering the Texans look to be improved on offense while their intimidating defense has regressed significantly in 2026. Hill's Pick: Over 38.5 (-110) The Dolphins are 0-4 but have been feisty and rather competitive the last couple of weeks against the Chiefs and Vikings. The heat in Miami is a tough obstacle for visitors this time of year. I like the home team to keep it close. Hill's Pick: Dolphins +7.5 (-110) The Patriots perhaps saved their season last week with a clutch win in Buffalo.

NFL Week 4 Quarterback Props NFL Week 4 Quarterback Prop Prediction #1 Jameis Winston New York Giants OVER 208.5 Passing Yards (-114) The New York Giants have been very conservative with Jameis Winston, and he’s finished with 118 and 111 passing yards, but we have to keep in mind that he didn’t start in Monday Night Football game against the Los Angeles Rams. Now Winston gets an opportunity against an Arizona Cardinals defense that ranks below average against the pass while allowing 247 yards per game and their two starting cornerbacks have an average PFF grade of 52.1. Jacoby Brissett and the Cardinals have been airing it out as they rank top 10 in pass frequency. We have seen all three opposing quarterbacks eclipse this number against Arizona including Brock Purdy (297), Drew Lock (235) and Justin Herbert (209). It’s time for Winston to go back to his roots as a gunslinger in what sets up as a low scoring game with a solid total of 44.5. NFL Week 4 Quarterback Prop Prediction #2 Jordan Love Green Bay Packers OVER 1.5 Touchdown Passes (+110) Jordan Love has thrown exactly two touchdown passes in each of his first two games of the season while averaging 281.3 passing yards per game. Without Josh Jacobs, the Green Bay Packers rushing attack has been non-existent as they rank DEAD LAST in rushing yards per attempt with only 3 yards per carry. The Tampa Bay Buccaneers run defense has been very stout as they rank 2nd with only 3.1 yards allowed per carry. Tampa Bay has only allowed four passing touchdowns through their first three games, but DeShaun Watson beat this line with two, and Kyler Murray and the Vikings led early on and kept things relatively conservative. Love and the Packers will find it easier to throw against a strong run defense and they have plenty of scoring options at their disposal. NFL Week 4 Running Back Props NFL Week 4 RB Prop Prediction #1 Jonathan Taylor Indianapolis Colts OVER 90.5 Rushing Yards (-112) Jonathan Taylor has covered this line in 2 of his first 3 games of the season with 68, 92 and 98 yards for an average of 86 yards per game. The Indianapolis Colts have only handed the ball of on 44% of their offensive snaps, but Taylor has still seen amazing volume with 23, 24 and 19 rushing attempts. Indianapolis has an elite offensive line that currently ranks 6th in run blocking according to PFF. The Washington Commanders did a solid job keeping the lid on Seattle Seahawk and Dallas Cowboy running backs, but Saquon Barkley did run for 83 yards against them in Week 1. However, Washington’s linebacker core has been bit by the injury bug as Leo Chenal is out for the season (neck) and Frankie Luvu is dealing with a nagging groin injury. This game will be played overseas in London, and the Colts find themselves as -3.5-point favorites which should set Taylor up with a positive game script. NFL Week 4 RB Prop Prediction #2 Chuba Hubbard Carolina Panthers OVER 18.5 Receiving Yards (-114) FD Chuba Hubbard has crushed this line in 2 of 3 games to open the 2026 NFL campaign with 28, 11 and 38 receiving yards (avg 25.7/game) despite only seeing 4, 2 and 3 targets. Those targets could increase in Week 4 as Xavier Legette is listed as doubtful and Jalen Coker is listed as questionable. The Detroit Lions rank 5th in blitz rate (42.6%) and Hubbard already thrived against a blitz happy Chicago Bears defense in a Week 1 (38 yards) game where his teammate Jonathan Brooks also logged a 48-yard reception in that contest. Brooks has already been ruled out for the remainder of the season and that leaves Hubbard as the Panthers only legitimate receiving threat out of the backfield. We have already seen two running backs beat this number as Breece Hall finished with 23 yards and Travis Etienne finished with 32 yards. NFL Week 4 Wide Receiver/Tight End Props NFL Week 4 TE Prop Prediction Jake Ferguson Dallas Cowboys OVER 23.5 Receiving Yards (-114) In the first three weeks of the season, Jake Ferguson has run 82 routes while playing 128 snaps and posting a 10.9% target share in the process. Those are solid numbers while competing with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens and Ferguson’s numbers are on the rise during the past two weeks while catching 7/9 targets for 66 yards. Now Ferguson draws an elite matchup against a Houston Texans defense that has allowed the 5th most yards (71/game) and 9th most receptions (6/game) to opposing tight ends. The Texans linebacking core is thin and most of their top coverage guys are banged up or ruled out for Week 4. We have already watched two tight ends absolutely torch Houston including Tyler Warren (55) and Dalton Kincaid (130). NFL Week 4 WR Prop Prediction Malik Washington Miami Dolphins OVER 37.5 Receiving Yards (-114) Malik Washington currently leads the Miami Dolphins in receiving yards (152), receptions (12) and targets (23) through the first three games of the season. More importantly to this particular play, Washington has covered this line in all three of those games with 56, 53 and 43 receiving yards. Now Washington will face off against a Minnesota Vikings defense that has allowed the 10th most receiving yards to opposing wide receivers with an average of 174 yards per game. We have already seen six opposing wide receivers eclipse this number against Minnesota including Emeka Egbuka (62), Ted Hurst III (40), Kalif Raymond (43), Rome Odunze (40), Matthew Golden (95) and Christian Watson (147). De’Von Achane is on the shelf due to an injury so there will be extra touches on the table, and the game script is perfect as the Dolphins sit as -10.5-point underdogs. NFL Week 4 Touchdown Props NFL Week 4 Anytime Touchdown Prop Prediction #1 James Cook III Buffalo Bills (-111) James Cook has scored in each of his last two games despite Josh Allen receiving 55.6% of the Buffalo Bills carries inside the five-yard line. Cook is the only other Bills player who has recorded a carry inside the five-yard line and Allen took a shot to the knee in Week 3 so he may be less likely to risk running in Week 4. Cook has scored a touchdown in 3 of his last 4 head-to-head meetings with the New England Patriots (6 total), and they just allowed both Bhayshul Tuten and Chris Rodriguez scored against them in a blowout loss in Jacksonville. Cook has posted a monster 22.6% explosive run rate, so he doesn’t necessarily need to rely on scoring from the red area. The Bills are -6.5-point home favorites in this contest and that sets Cook up with an ideal game script to find the end zone. NFL Week 4 Anytime Touchdown Prop Prediction #2 Brock Bowers Las Vegas Raiders (+185) Brock Bowers had an amazing first game his 2026 campaign where he caught 10 of 13 targets for 116 yards and a touchdown against the New Orleans Saints. In that game, Bowers saw three red area targets while posting a 39.4% target share. Now Bowers gets an opportunity to expose a Kansas City Chiefs defense that has already allowed touchdowns to tight ends Evan Engram and Tyler Warren to score in 2026. The last time Bowers faced Kansas City was back in 2024 and he caught 10 of 14 targets for 140 yards and a touchdown despite playing on the road. Now he’s at home in an indoor game as a -4.5-point underdog which sets up for a pass heavy game script. Rueben Bain Jr. to be a Top 10 pick: Yes ( -162 ) “Miami Hurricanes EDGE Rueben Bain Jr. has 30.9-inch arms, which likely cause him to slide, but I don't think he can get past eight overall to the New Orleans Saints or nine overall to the Kansas City Chiefs. The 21-year-old finished fifth in the ACC with 7.5 sacks as a freshman, before regressing somewhat as a sophomore while battling injuries. Bain Jr. then returned to form this past year, setting career-highs in tackles (54), tackles for loss (15.5), and sacks (9.5), while leading the Hurricanes to a College Football Playoff (CFP) National Championship appearance. This earned him AP Consensus All-America and ACC Defensive Player of the Year honors, as well as the Ted Hendricks Award. Those accomplishments, a high character, and elite film should be enough to keep him inside the top 10 picks, making this arguably the best prop bet available.” – Seth Woolcock ( FantasyPros ) Jacob Rodriguez drafted inside the top-32 ( +500 ) “I’m a sucker for the “Will this player be drafted in Round 1″ betting market. Right now, my favorite approach is to select Texas Tech LB Jacob Rodriguez inside the top-32 at 5-1 odds. He’s been a buzzy late 1st-round pick across several sources (Tony Pauline) and has been tied to several teams between picks 15-32, such as Dallas, Houston, Miami, Buffalo, Pittsburgh, Tampa Bay, New England, and Chicago.” – Andrew Erickson ( FantasyPros ) Who will be the fourth overall pick? “Arvell Reese ( +650 at DraftKings ) or Sonny Styles ( +175 at BetMGM ) — The info/draft rumors I hear about change literally by the minute. By the time you read this, things might be drastically different, but here goes nothing. (FYI- at the time of this writing, it’s Wednesday night, 10:30 p.m.) Anyway, it sounds like Arizona’s owner, Michael Bidwell, might veto GM Monte Ossenfort’s wishes to trade out of the third pick. The rumor is that Ossenfort apparently either wants Edge David Bailey if he’s there or to trade it for more picks if the Jets select Bailey. However, Bidwell wants Jeremiyah Love because he would add some excitement to the Cardinals’ fan base and could help sell some tickets. So, if you think Arizona keeps the pick and selects Love, I think the best way to play that would be to bet the Titans to select Arvell Reese and Sonny Styles. I don’t think Titans’ head coach Robert Saleh (who is a former defensive coordinator) would take Love, Carnell Tate, or Jordyn Tyson over a good prospect on defense, even if he slips. And if Arizona picks Love, you essentially get a free roll with Reese, assuming the Titans don’t trade the pick. Worth a shot.” – Mark Ringo ( Sleepers and Busts ) Carnell Tate drafted in Top 7 ( +105 ) “Carnell Tate’s draft position u7.5 ( +105 at DraftKings ). I’m surprised this bet hasn’t been steamed, but it could be by the time you read this. I’ll grab this bet and take it anywhere I can find it for plus money. Tate’s floor right now looks like seventh overall to the Commanders, and I wouldn’t be shocked if he went as high as fourth overall to the Titans.” – Derek Brown ( FantasyPros ) Fewer than 8.5 SEC players drafted in First Round ( -185 ) “You’ll make money if you bet that there will be fewer than 8.5 players from SEC schools selected in the first round (-185). Normally, the first round of the draft is littered with SEC guys. Not this year. Mansoor Delane (LSU), Kadyn Proctor (Alabama), and Keldric Faulk (Auburn) are the SEC’s only first-round locks, and K.C. Concepcion (Texas A&M) is a near-lock. That’s four. Allen (Georgia, and Caleb Banks (Florida) are first-round possibilities. There’s a decent chance one of these players makes it into the first round. I don’t think we’ll see two or more players from this group make it, and if we do get more than one, it could very well be at the expense of McCoy, Hood, or Simpson.” – Pat Fitzmaurice ( FantasyPros ) Carnell Tate to be first WR drafted ( -180 ) “Carnell Tate is the betting favorite to be the first wide receiver selected in the 2026 NFL Draft at -180 odds, largely due to his exceptional route running and ‘pro-ready’ profile.
